title: 2005 AMC 8 Problem 3
statement: What is the minimum number of small squares that must be shaded so that a line of symmetry lies on the diagonal \(\overline{BD}\) of square \(ABCD\)?

solutions.text:
For diagonal \(\overline{BD}\) to be a line of symmetry, every shaded square off the diagonal must have a matching reflected shaded square on the other side of the diagonal.

There are \(4\) shaded squares whose reflected partners are not shaded, so \(4\) additional small squares must be shaded.

Thus, D is the correct answer.
hints: Reflect the shaded squares across diagonal \(\overline{BD}\).
Only shaded squares without a matching reflected square need to be paired.
